findings_resolved: Scientific science --task-key and original flag ordering are preserved through wrapper dispatch
Readiness requires exact PID, recipe, random launch nonce, atomic patch and successful actual queue observation
Busy scheduler or queue-query retry cannot claim first observation success or submit in initial cycle
Repeated current controller startup before or after lock acquisition does not duplicate or restart it
Installer does not forward an unsupported unused credentials argument
Successful fresh controller readiness is written identically to repair work and original runtime metadata so GitHub reports the current repaired PID rather than stale bootstrap state
verified_behaviors: Screenshot-shaped missing temporary rename is reproduced; private same-filesystem staged writer retries bounded transient I/O and retains old target on permanent failure
Four concurrent process writes produce only whole parseable JSON; cleanup never sweeps foreign temporary files
Monitoring-only status/observation errors do not terminate production persistent worker; durable result/completion/tasks/scheduler writes stay strict
Known monitor-induced blocked tasks recover only under task lease and scientific lock; complete artifacts fully hash verified before sealing without recomputation
Incomplete known-monitor failures retain payload and failure history for retry; unrelated blocked tasks are untouched; active scientific locks are never stolen
Original scheduler first reconciles exact marker, persisted intents and fake queue/accounting; two running allocations are retained and only two ended slots are replaced
Owned controller identity requires same UID, actual script position and controller mode, exact authorized plan bytes and process start ticks; workers/science/upload/foreign scripts are rejected
Only identified operational controller PID is signalled in fixtures; never a process group or scientific worker
Default installer performs no subprocess/network/numerical import and verifies all packaged byte hashes; explicit --repair --submit remains required for resume
limitations: All Slurm/process/signal actions exercised with local fixtures; no school SSH or live worker control
The exact external/filesystem reason a temporary rename source vanished is not proven
Existing live original worker processes cannot receive an in-memory patch retroactively; they remain alive and any ended slot is replaced with the new wrapper
A ready controller acknowledges queue observation, not immediate GPU availability or scientific completion
School completed-result recovery and resumed numerical progress must be confirmed from school receipts after apply
